title: Publish fresh record candidates as coherent transactions
description: Publish the exact explicit replacement set after current identity and structural checks while excluding competing supported writers and preserving recoverability. It owns storage publication, not the validity of the actor's engineering judgment or arbitrary repository edits.
inputs: Exact candidate write set, expected revision/target identities, and actor-declared decision-basis identities.
Selected change and coherent current registered state, including explicit absence for permitted creation.
outputs: Saved or unchanged result with actual resulting revision and affected identities.
Conflict, busy, rejection, or recovery-required outcome identifying the bounded storage result.
behavior: Apply shared containment and identity protection on every supported publication path, including observed ancestor substitution and exact selected-change allowlists.
Acquire the common supported-writer exclusion, read current coherent state, check expected revision, targets and declared basis, and validate the complete candidate before publication.
Check revision before no-op recognition: fresh identical content is unchanged; an old-revision retry conflicts even if prior publication succeeded.

Prepare exact before/candidate recovery information before authoritative replacement, publish the related set as one logical transaction, and report saved only when all requested bytes are durably committed.
Expose coherent before/after snapshots or busy/recovery-required to supported readers; never publish an intermediate candidate as usable current state.

Recheck declared decision-basis identities at the required observed points, restoring safely or requiring recovery after detected drift, without claiming atomic exclusion of outside edits after the final check.

failure_behavior.condition: Expected state or declared basis differs at an observed check, or a supported writer already owns publication.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report conflict or busy without merging decisions, refreshing expectations, or overwriting the winning work.

failure_behavior.condition: Publication or its final checks are interrupted or cannot reach a verified committed state.
failure_behavior.outcome: Retain verified recovery information and expose recovery-required rather than saved or a usable mixed snapshot.
